articleTitle: Simulation modelling of flexible manufacturing systems
abstract: The elements of a flexible manufacturing system include workstations, load/unload stations, transport, pallets, fixtures, tools, buffer/store and control computer. In embarking on a simulation the system should be defined and the model validated. A stochastic discrete next event simulation is usually used. Simulation provides system behaviour prior to its construction or provides non-invasive study of an existing system and produces awareness of the problem as well as a communication aid. The author discusses the development of manufacturing simulation and performance maximisation.

articleTitle: An integrated approach to computer simulation of casting processes
abstract: The casting process combines many complex physical phenomena. With recent increases in computing speeds and reductions in the cost of machines, it is becoming viable to model even the most complex physical processes. The UK casting industry, supported by the UK Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in its Castings Initiative, has been developing a flexible approach to computer modelling of casting processes. The Casting Initiative is promoting work in both the development of software and of verification of software and methods. A core computer program is being developed by FEGS Ltd to provide a user-friendly casting-specific front end and a common link between different solution packages. An environment has been developed that includes a modified version of DYNA3D, TOPAZ3D and a number of other controlling programs. This software environment is referred to in this paper as CAST3D. It is essential that any software for the simulation of casting should be validated. CAST3D and a number of other commercial codes are being extensively verified in a three year program of parallel testing and simulation. This paper addresses the following three subjects: the UK DTI's Casting Initiative; a framework approach to coordinate pre- and post-processing and solving software, implemented by FEGS Ltd; and DYNA3D extended for use in the simulation of casting processes.

articleTitle: Manufacturing systems simulation with enhanced visualisation using virtual reality techniques
abstract: The paper discusses SWOOPVR which is a combination of the SWOOP mixed-mode industrial simulation language and VROOM virtual reality package, both developed at the University of Sheffield. SWOOP is a simulation toolbox that runs under Turbo Pascal and allows the simulation of both discrete and continuous systems. On its own it allows simulation output as numerical data, statistical summaries, time-based graphs or high quality two-dimensional animation. The paper discusses some manufacturing applications of the package.

articleTitle: User performance evaluation of a pipeline based production control system
abstract: The paper examines the dynamic performance evaluation of an automatic pipeline, inventory and order based production control system (APIOBPCS) via the use of simulation. Model outputs of particular interest to the system users are finished goods stock levels, production output and work-in-progress (WIP). The major players with interests in the evaluation of an APIOBPCS include the inventory manager who puts a high priority on controlling stock levels, the production manager who wants effective control over the factory output and the production scheduler who needs accurate WIP information and utilisation to ensure that the system "pipeline" is full. A systems engineering methodology is introduced that examines all three measures and their total contribution to the dynamic performance of a system. A version of the multi attribute utility technology (MAUT) known as SMART (Simple Multi Attribute Rating Technique) is utilised in deriving a unified performance index.

articleTitle: An intelligent architecture for the simulation of product quality in a machining centre
abstract: The paper presents an intelligent architecture based synergistic fuzzy timed Petri nets and a neural network for simulating product quality in a CNC machining centre. It describes how the proposed architecture can be utilised for modelling, monitoring and control of a product quality specification such as surface finish. The surface finish represents the output quality characteristic manufactured by a CNC machining centre as a result of a milling process. The neural network structure simulates and models the selected input milling parameters in order to identify the demanded quality. The synergistic approach uses two fuzzy timed Petri nets and a fuzzy timed Petri net combiner to simulate and model the actual milling parameters to identify the quality of surface finish. In addition, a fuzzy timed Petri net expert employed in order to model and simulate the final quality of surface finish as high, medium or low.

articleTitle: Manufacturing simulation in the aircraft industry
abstract: British Aerospace's Chadderton factory was established in 1937 to manufacture large military aircraft and it continued to specialise in these until the declining market for them forced a change towards civil aircraft manufacture. The paper discusses the application of manufacturing simulation at BAe Chadderton. It considers the selection and cost-justification of new plant and equipment.

The author argues that manufacturing simulation could be a relatively simple form of programming if there were a common vocabulary of manufacturing terms whose definitions and detailed terminology were widely agreed. This would greatly assist modelling, and also the comparison of alternatives both in measurements and in costs.
